cards.text: John, who's been seeing these visions, just ate a small scroll and was told to prophesy again. Now he's handed a measuring rod like a staff, and friend, measuring is my WHOLE career. I've been pressing every cookie the exact same size since before you were born!

cards.question: John's holding the measuring rod. What's he told to go and measure?

answers.text: The temple of God and the altar
The walls and gates of the city
The tents of the camp of Israel

cards.question: Along with measuring, John is told to count the number of worshipers there.
John is told to leave one part of the temple unmeasured. Which part?

answers.text: The steps up to the altar

cards.question: John skips the courtyard outside the temple because it's too holy to be measured.

cards.text: Nope. The courtyard has been given over to the nations, and they'll trample the holy city for 42 months.
Then the one speaking promises to empower two witnesses, who will prophesy for 1,260 days. 1,260 DAYS, baker, and I used to think my double shifts at the oven were long!

cards.question: The two witnesses are about to prophesy for 1,260 days. What are they clothed in?
John says the two witnesses stand before the Lord of the earth. They are the two ___ trees and the two ___.

cards.text: Now listen to me. These two are NOT the ones you want to pick a fight with.

cards.question: What happens if anyone wants to harm the two witnesses?

answers.text: Fire comes out of their mouths
The ground opens up beneath them

cards.question: The two witnesses have power to shut the sky so that no rain falls during the days of their prophecy.
The two witnesses have power over water too. They can turn the waters into ___.

cards.text: And they can strike the earth with every kind of plague, as often as they wish. Baker, the most power anybody had in my old junk drawer was the dead batteries, and they couldn't even run a flashlight.
The two witnesses carry out their testimony. But when they finish it, something comes up from the Abyss to wage war with them.

cards.question: What comes up from the Abyss to wage war with the two witnesses?
The beast overpowers and kills the two witnesses.

cards.text: Their bodies lie in the street of the great city, the one figuratively called Sodom and Egypt.

cards.question: The great city where the witnesses' bodies lie gets one more description. What is it?

answers.text: Where their Lord was also crucified
Where the ark of God was captured
Where King David was first anointed

cards.text: For three and a half days, all peoples and tribes and tongues and nations look at their bodies.

cards.question: During those three and a half days, the people let the two witnesses be laid in a tomb.
How do those who dwell on the earth react to the deaths of the two witnesses?

answers.text: They gloat and send one another gifts
They mourn and cover themselves in ashes
They hide in caves and among the rocks

cards.question: The people of the earth celebrate because these two prophets had ___ them.

cards.text: So this crowd is throwing a full celebration, gifts and everything. And then, after the three and a half days... friend. Wait for it.

cards.question: After the three and a half days, what enters the two witnesses?

answers.text: The breath of life from God
A burning coal from the altar
A light from the throne of God

cards.question: When the two witnesses stand on their feet, the people watching cheer even louder.

cards.text: Great fear falls on everyone who sees them. Picture it, baker: you're mid-party, passing out gifts, and the whole reason for the party STANDS UP. I'd drop every cookie box I was holding. EVERY one. With my mustache AND my dignity.

cards.question: A loud voice from heaven calls out to the two witnesses. Where do they go as their enemies watch?

answers.text: Up to heaven in a cloud

cards.text: "Come up here." That's all the voice says, and up they go. And in that hour, a great earthquake hits the city.

cards.question: In the great earthquake, a ___ of the city collapses.

cards.text: Seven thousand are killed in the quake. Now watch the ones who are left.

cards.question: What do the rest of the people in the city do after the great earthquake?

answers.text: They are terrified and give glory to God
They curse God and refuse to repent
They flee to the mountains and hide

cards.text: Then comes this line: "The second woe has passed. Behold, the third woe is coming shortly."
And then the seventh angel sounds his trumpet, and loud voices call out in heaven. Baker, this is the trumpet. THE trumpet. I got goosebumps on my gold base.

cards.question: The seventh trumpet sounds and loud voices fill heaven. What do they announce?

answers.text: The world's kingdom has become the Lord's
The holy city has been measured again
The great city has been rebuilt for good

cards.question: The loud voices in heaven say He will reign for a thousand years.

cards.text: Forever and ever, friend. Then the twenty-four elders who sit on their thrones before God respond.

cards.question: After the seventh trumpet, what do the twenty-four elders do?

answers.text: Fall on their faces and worship God
Stand up and sound their own trumpets
Rise and leave their thrones in fear

cards.text: As they worship, they say, "We give thanks to You, O Lord God Almighty, the One who is and who was" and they're not done.

cards.question: Why do the twenty-four elders give thanks to the Lord God Almighty?

cards.text: The elders keep going. The nations were enraged, they say, and God's wrath has come.

cards.question: The elders say the time has come to ___ the dead and to ___ God's servants the prophets.
The elders say the reward is also for the saints and those who fear God's name, both small and great.

cards.text: Small AND great, baker. That means a 25-cent stamper from a bargain bin is on the list too. And the elders name one more thing: the time has come to destroy those who destroy the earth.
Then the temple of God in heaven is opened. I've waited by an oven door my whole life, friend, but THIS door?

cards.question: When God's temple in heaven is opened, the ___ of His covenant appears.

cards.text: And heaven doesn't open quietly.

cards.question: What comes along with the opening of God's temple in heaven?

answers.text: Silence for about half an hour

findings.problem: The card states facts from Revelation 10 (John ate a small scroll and was told to prophesy again), but it cites only Revelation 11:1. The outside fact has no reference.

rule.text: Facts from outside the passage are fine when they help, like who a new person is or who wrote a letter, with their reference.

findings.problem: "Since before you were born" assumes the baker's age. Papa Dorin isn't told anything about the individual baker.

rule.text: anything about the individual baker that he hasn't been told, such as their streak, their mood, the time of day or how they've done before.

findings.problem: The question calls the courtyard "one part of the temple." Revelation 11:2 calls it "the courtyard outside the temple."

rule.text: Call things what the text calls them.

findings.problem: The question types in Stop 2 start with the same sequence as Stop 1: multiple choice, true or false, multiple choice, true or false, multiple choice, fill in the blank, multiple choice, true or false. Both stops also mostly alternate multiple choice and true or false, which is a pattern.

rule.text: Which question type comes next, the order the types come in and where a blank falls are chosen naturally for each card. They never follow a pattern. No stop repeats another stop's pattern, and no type dominates a stop by a wide margin.

findings.problem: The card is 3 sentences. Its first sentence also recaps the celebration already covered on card 8, instead of moving the passage forward.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The first sentence, "So this crowd is throwing a full celebration, gifts and everything," repeats what the baker answered on card 8.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.
Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The story card is 3 sentences and has two beats: the joke and a new fact from verse 18 (destroying those who destroy the earth).

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: "He" in "say He will reign" points back to the Lord and His Christ, who were named only in card 3's answer. That answer is no longer on screen.

rule.text: Always give context in the question. The story card before it isn't on screen anymore, so the question says who and what. Never "him," "that" or "it" pointing back to a card the baker can't see.

findings.problem: The false statement "He will reign for a thousand years" echoes Revelation 20:4-6. Marking it False is accurate for 11:15, but bakers who know Revelation 20 may read it as denying the thousand-year reign. That touches end-times views that differ between denominations.
findings.question: Should wrong answers in Revelation avoid using details that appear elsewhere in Revelation and are tied to disputed end-times views, like the thousand years?
